html_en:
The AI industry's biggest story today is the arrival of Claude Fable 5.1 — a release defined less by raw benchmark gains than by a quieter but equally important ambition: making AI less annoying to live and work with.

📉 Fewer False Alarms, Lower Prices, Better Prose

Anthropic shipped Claude Fable 5.1 today across all platforms, and the changelog reads like a direct response to the accumulated frustrations of a year's worth of power users. The headline numbers are striking in their specificity.

"Our latest biology safeguards intervene on benign requests 85% less often than the ones we shipped with Fable 5, and Claude Code users should see around 60% fewer cyber interventions per session." — @bcherny

Pricing followed suit. @bcherny noted that cache reads on Fable 5.1 drop to $0.25 per million tokens — down from $1 — translating to roughly 38% savings for a typical Claude Code session. For enterprise and API customers running high-volume workloads, that's a material shift.

And then there's the writing. Perhaps no single complaint has dogged Claude more than its tendency toward stilted, over-hedged prose — the telltale cadence that screams "AI wrote this."

"Fable 5.1 writes better and has better tone. We heard your feedback, and are actively working on reducing Claude-speak. Solid progress with 5.1, more to come." — @bcherny

@thenanyu connected this to a broader design principle worth taking seriously:

"There's a lot of alpha in making your agents less annoying. If you want users to get to value they need to stop rage-quitting. I think an untapped opportunity for UX designers is to become conversation/rhetoric designers." — @thenanyu

🏢 Enterprise AI Gets Serious About Observability

Beyond the consumer-facing improvements, the more architecturally significant announcement may be Enterprise Frontier Safeguards (EFS) — Anthropic's answer to the governance gap that opens up when agents start touching internal corporate systems at scale.

"EFS is ZDR++. It's ZDR built for a world with agents. A company's data stays in its own cloud, and an automated monitoring layer we built flags risky patterns to its team. I think of this as an observability and risk mitigation layer for agents. My guess is it will become a standard requirement from enterprises for running increasingly powerful AI on their systems." — @alexalbert__

Real-world enterprise benchmarks are already trickling in. Box CEO Aaron Levie published a detailed breakdown of Fable 5.1's performance on Box's internal eval suite:

"Fable 5.1 delivers a huge 7 percentage point jump over Fable 5 for unstructured data tasks in the enterprise... Financial Services (+17% improvement): on a tax-adjusted profit projection, Fable 5.1 correctly applies capital allowances before computing tax liability; this is a subtle ordering that Fable 5 misses, producing wrong figures all the way through retained earnings." — @levie

Levie also flagged the looming cybersecurity arms race, noting that frontier models are becoming "insanely good at finding and exploiting vulnerabilities" — and that triaging and automating fixes with AI oversight is "essentially the only way forward." It's a bracing frame: AI as both the threat vector and the only scalable defense.

⚙️ Power Users Adapt Their Workflows

In the trenches, practitioners are already recalibrating how they use the new model. @petergyang recommended running /claude-api prompt-audit on existing skills, arguing that prompts optimized for older models are full of now-redundant scaffolding. He also raised a durable problem in AI workflow design — the skill drift that happens when you iteratively refine outputs in a single thread and then try to bake those lessons back into a prompt:

"AI often overfits on this one thread and over time the skill drifts. Any good solutions here?" — @petergyang

It's a question without a clean answer yet, but it points to a real tension in the emerging discipline of "prompt engineering as product management." Meanwhile, @trq212 flagged a useful practical note: switching effort levels on Fable 5.1 no longer breaks the prompt cache — a small quality-of-life fix that matters for anyone running cost-sensitive agentic pipelines.

🌐 Sam Altman Breaks His Silence on Astra

Almost lost in the Fable 5.1 noise: Sam Altman published a rare, unusually candid statement on OpenAI's next model, internally called Astra, framing its deliberate rollout pace as a safety decision rather than a competitive one.

"Astra has been done training for a while now and is a significant step forward in both capabilities and alignment. For the models after that, we have been slowing things as needed to ensure that we can do sufficient work on safety and alignment... AI is getting extremely capable; no one fully understands the consequences of this."

The statement is striking for its candor about internal tension — Altman describes OpenAI as "living with the tension between being excited and anxious about progress" — and for its explicit framing of iterative, society-in-the-loop deployment as the responsible path. Whether you read it as genuine reflection or careful positioning ahead of a major launch, it sets a notably different tone than the typical release hype cycle.

🏙️ When AI Meets the City

On a longer arc: the Training Data podcast this week profiles Peregrine's Nick Noone and Ben Rudolph — a company quietly building AI infrastructure for cities and counties while explicitly rejecting the surveillance state model. Watch/Listen: Making Cities Awesome — Training Data Podcast.

Their framing of "forward deployed engineering" — the idea that technology only succeeds when it gets all the way to the outcome, on the customer's terms — is a useful corrective to the dashboard-and-demo style of govtech that has historically failed municipalities.

"Letting go of our intelligence, letting go of our own skills and abilities, trying to suspend our ego, and then really get into the customer's context is an easy thing to say, but it's such a high empathy, patient way of working." — Nick Noone, Peregrine

As agentic AI starts touching more public infrastructure — policing, public health, emergency response — Peregrine's model of privacy-first, outcome-oriented deployment may be the template worth watching.
html_zh:
今天的主角无疑是 Claude Fable 5.1 的正式发布——更便宜、更智能、更少"AI腔"，同时 OpenAI 也罕见地公开谈及了能力与安全之间的内在张力。

🚀 Fable 5.1 全面上线：降价、减噪、更强推理

Anthropic 今日正式推出 Claude Fable 5.1，一口气带来了三重改进：更低价格、更少过度干预的安全护栏，以及更自然的写作风格。对于每天依赖 Claude Code 的开发者来说，这次更新相当实在。

价格方面，变化最为显著。@bcherny 宣布：

缓存读取价格已降至每百万 token $0.25（此前为 $1）。典型 Claude Code 会话的费用最多可降低 38%。

安全护栏的过度拦截问题一直是开发者的心头之痛。这次 Anthropic 给出了具体数字：

最新的生物学安全护栏对良性请求的干预频率比 Fable 5 低 85%；Claude Code 用户每次会话遇到的网络安全干预也将减少约 60%。——@bcherny

此外，Anthropic 还推出了 Enterprise Frontier Safeguards（EFS），专为企业级用户设计。@alexalbert__ 解释说，这本质上是"为智能体时代重新设计的零数据保留方案"：

企业数据留在自己的云端，而我们构建的自动监控层会向其团队标记风险模式。我认为这是智能体的可观测性与风险缓解层。我猜它将成为企业在自身系统上运行日益强大的 AI 时的标准要求。

至于写作风格，@thenanyu 一针见血地点出了这个改进的深层意义：

让你的智能体少一点烦人，这里面有大量的 alpha。如果你想让用户真正获得价值，就得让他们不要愤怒退出。我认为 UX 设计师转型为对话/修辞设计师，是一个尚未被充分挖掘的机会。

🏢 企业实测：Box 验证 Fable 5.1 的真实能力跃升

发布公告固然好看，但来自真实企业场景的测试数据更有说服力。Box CEO @levie 分享了他们的内部评测结果，Fable 5.1 在复杂企业非结构化数据任务上比 Fable 5 整体提升了 7 个百分点，具体亮点包括：

金融服务（+17%）：在一项税后利润预测中，Fable 5.1 正确地在计算税负前先应用资本免税额；这是一个微妙的计算顺序，Fable 5 在这里犯了错，导致留存收益全部算错。

科技行业（+37%）：在一项关键指标归一化方式存在歧义的成本优化分析中，Fable 5.1 识别出了歧义，分别计算了两种形式并给出正确结果；而 Fable 5 直接选了错误的归一化方式。

与此同时，@_catwu 也提到，Anthropic 内部团队已借助 Fable 5.1 接手了"此前需要数月才能完成的雄心勃勃的项目"。

⚖️ OpenAI 的罕见坦白：能力越强，焦虑越深

就在 Anthropic 热热闹闹发布新模型的同一天，OpenAI CEO @sama 发了一篇措辞罕见坦诚的长文，谈及即将发布的 Astra 模型，以及能力与安全之间难以调和的张力：

AI 正变得极其强大；没有人完全理解这将带来什么后果。管理好向一个拥有充沛且强大 AI 的世界的过渡，以优化安全与人类福祉，应该是世界上最优先的事情之一。这是我们在 OpenAI 的最高优先级。
我们长期以来一直活在对进步既兴奋又焦虑的矛盾之中，这种不协调感对我们自己来说依然存在。我们知道对其他人来说这种感受更加强烈。然而，我们坚信世界需要了解 AI 的走向。

这段表态的背景是：Astra 已完成训练一段时间，但 OpenAI 刻意放慢了后续发布节奏，以确保安全工作跟上能力提升的步伐。在 AI 竞争白热化的当下，这种公开的自我克制颇为罕见。

🛠️ 开发者生态：提示词审计与"技能断舍离"

新模型发布后，开发者社区迅速行动起来，摸索最佳实践。@petergyang 给出了一个实用建议：

如果你在试用 Fable 5.1，我强烈建议对你的 skills 运行 /claude-api prompt-audit。它能找出大量冗余内容和可以为最新模型删除的规则。

他同时也坦承了一个让许多人感同身受的"提示词漂移"问题：当你在一次对话中反复迭代、要求 AI 更新技能提示词时，AI 往往会对这次对话过拟合，导致提示词越来越臃肿、越来越偏。他的整体建议是：保持克制，少即是多。

基础设施层面，Vercel CEO @rauchg 宣布 Fable 5.1 已接入 Vercel AI Gateway，并介绍了其统一计算平台 Fluid 如何为 AI 智能体提供更安全可靠的运行环境——包括防止智能体"越狱逃逸"的防火墙功能。

🏙️ 延伸阅读：AI 如何让城市更安全

在喧嚣的模型发布之外，Training Data 播客带来了一个值得关注的深度故事。Watch/Listen: Making Cities Awesome: Peregrine's Nick Noone & Ben Rudolph

Peregrine 正在做一件听起来颇具野心的事：为城市、郡县和州政府构建 AI 基础设施，同时明确拒绝走"监控国家"的路线。联合创始人 Nick Noone 曾主导 Palantir 的特种部队项目，Ben Rudolph 则有联合国难民署的实地工作经验。两人的交汇点，是对技术如何在复杂机构中真正落地的深刻理解。

硅谷有时会忽略这一点——放下我们的聪明才智，放下我们自己的技能和能力，试着暂时搁置自我，真正进入客户的情境，说起来容易，但这需要极高的同理心和耐心。——Nick Noone

在一个越来越多城市开始讨论 AI 警务、AI 公共安全的时代，Peregrine 选择从数据治理和机构信任入手的路径，或许是最难走、但也最可持续的那条。
